title: Backpressure sentinel and graceful model failover playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a production-ready 'Backpressure Sentinel' that derives per-dependency / per-model / per-tenant trip curves from SLOs and traffic characteristics, performs predictive load-shedding, and executes deterministic safe fallbacks across regions. Deliverables: (1) algorithm to map SLOs + latency/error distribution -> trip thresholds with hysteresis, (2) runtime sentinel that applies soft backpressure (probabilistic reject, throttled queueing) before hard trip, (3) automatic fallback routing to cached responses, smaller quantized models, or regional replicas, (4) observability/dashboarding for trip events and customer impact, (5) canary + rollout + test harness and playbook for on-call. Rationale: Recent incidents showed tight tail latency spikes from model dependencies causing cascading QPS amplification and delayed KV-cache eviction. We need deterministic, SLO-aligned protection that minimizes opaque 500s and preserves graceful degradations for high-value tenants.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Kickoff: briefed on postmortem and agreed scope. Stakeholders: SRE, Runtime, Product. Action: prototype threshold derivation by Mar 8. (Aisha)

2026-03-03 - Architecture proposal posted: use a two-stage sentinel: a probabilistic backpressure layer (soft) + a configurable tripper (hard) with regional affinity and tenant weighting. Proposed signals: p95/p99 latency, error-rate, queue-depth growth. (Liam)

2026-03-05 - Prototype results: simulated workload with mixed-tenant QPS. Soft backpressure reduced observed hard trips by ~62% and cut tail tokens served by the heavy model by 37% while keeping latency SLOs for high-tier tenants. Experimental config stored at runtime/configs/backpressure-experiment-2026-03.json. (Eng prototyping)

2026-03-06 - Design decision: map trip threshold to SLO as a composite score: score = alpha*latency_violation_rate + beta*error_rate + gamma*queue_growth. Tunable hysteresis window = 30s base. Chosen default alpha=0.6,beta=0.3,gamma=0.1. Rationale: prioritize latency SLOs but be sensitive to sudden error bursts. (Decision by SRE+Runtime)

2026-03-07 - Review feedback from PM (Jordan Kim): add customer-tier exceptions: high-tier customers get longer grace and lower probabilistic rejection rates; free-tier default to aggressive shedding. Also requested audit events for compliance. (Jordan)
2026-03-08 - Security review note: no plaintext secrets. Fallback routing uses existing signed tokens for region hops. Confirmed with Security that KMS patterns already in place. (Nina S.)

2026-03-09 - Implementation progress: sentinel shim implemented in runtime v1.23 branch. Integrations: trace spans, trip event metric (sentinel.trip.count), per-tenant reject-rate gauge. Current blocker: deterministic fallback policy needs consistent model-variant affinity table exposed by model-catalog service. Working with ModelOnboarding team. (Liam)

2026-03-10 - QA checklist: add unit tests for trip-curve math, integration test with canary region, chaos test for delayed regional links, and replay tests using recorded traffic from Feb incident. Assigned to test owner: Maya R. (Aisha)

Follow-ups: expand runbook with explicit API error payloads for 'soft-shed' responses (structured code SED-100) so clients can surface degraded-state UX instead of generic 500s. Add GDPR audit field to trip events.
decision_log: Prefer soft backpressure (probabilistic rejection + token-bucket slow-down) to immediate hard trips to allow smoothing and avoid thundering fallbacks.
Trip thresholds derived from SLO alignment rather than static qps thresholds; allows per-tenant customization and auto-recalibration based on recent distribution windows.

Fallback hierarchy: 1) local KV cache hit return, 2) quantized model variant pinned for tenant, 3) regional replica in same continent, 4) degrade to short-form answer with explicit 'degraded' flag. Avoid opaque error codes.

Rollout strategy: dark-launch sentinel in all regions for 1 week, then canary enable for 10% of traffic (low-tier default) for 48h, observe error/latency deltas, then expand using linear ramp if no regression.
Metric set required: sentinel.trip.count, sentinel.soft_shed.rate, sentinel.hysteresis.duration, per-tenant-latency-pctiles, fallback-rate-by-variant, end-to-end SLO slippage per 1h window.
